newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rest of Lufthansa sale to start in autumn.
newsitem.headline: Rest of Lufthansa sale to start in autumn.

text.p: The sale of the remaining state-held chunk of German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG will begin in the autumn, the government development agency Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau (KfW) said on Wednesday.

Gert Vogt, management board chairman of the KfW, said at the group's results conference that the flotation of at least a part of the Lufthansa stake, which Bonn has placed with the KfW, was planned for the autumn.
One of the conditions for the sale of the remainder of the airline is that 50 percent of the group remain in the hands of German shareholders post privatisation.
The provision is part of a ruling called LuftNaSIG which comes into force on July 1 1997.
In December 1996 the German government placed its remaining 35.68 percent stake in Lufthansa with the KfW for around 2.1 billion marks ($1.2 billion).
